title: だ (plain copula)
simpleExplanation: だ is the plain (casual) version of です. Both mean "is / am / are". You use だ with close friends and family, in diaries, and inside longer sentences. One important rule: だ goes after nouns and な-adjectives only. An い-adjective is already a complete plain sentence by itself (高い = "it is expensive"), so you never say 高いだ.
whenUsed: Casual conversation with friends, family and children; plain-style writing such as diaries and novels; and, most importantly for N5, inside sentences before と思う, でしょう, んです and から (学生だと思う "I think he is a student"). In everyday casual speech だ is often dropped: 学生。／ 静か。
formation: い-adjective + (nothing)  (高い — never 高いだ)
Negative: じゃない ／ Past: だった

examples.reading: たなかさんは せんせいだ。
examples.note: Noun + だ: the casual way to say 先生です.

examples.reading: きょうは やすみだ。
examples.note: 休み (day off) is a noun, so it takes だ.

examples.reading: この まちは しずかだ。
examples.note: 静か is a な-adjective; it takes だ just like a noun.

examples.ja: あの人は田中さんだと思います。
examples.reading: あの ひとは たなかさんだと おもいます。
examples.en: I think that person is Mr Tanaka.
examples.note: Inside と思います you must use the plain だ, even in a polite sentence.
い-adjective: the plain sentence ends with い and nothing else. 暑いだ is wrong.

similarGrammar.difference: The polite version. Same meaning; です is used with people you are not close to.
Not a copula, but the most common place where N5 forces you to use だ: 学生だと思います.

commonMistakes.why: い-adjectives never take だ. The い ending already makes a complete plain sentence.

commonMistakes.wrong: 田中さんは学生と思います。
commonMistakes.right: 田中さんは学生だと思います。
commonMistakes.why: Before と思う a noun needs だ. Without it the sentence sounds broken to a native speaker.
です and だ are two versions of the same word; choose one.

usageNotes: In casual speech だ is often dropped entirely (学生。/ 静か。). You must know the plain forms because they appear before と思う, でしょう, んです, and inside relative clauses.
jlptTips: N5 tests だ mostly indirectly: 〜だと思います, 〜だから, 〜でしょう (no だ!). Learn which patterns need だ and which forbid it.
If an option adds だ after an い-adjective (おいしいだ, 高いだと思う), it is always wrong.
